NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This is the first, deliberately small successor slice of the archived `C-MINT-BASELINE-CONTROL-1-5202CCD1`. The predecessor first drafted three removals at once: the historical mint control, the `validateJobCheckoutDepth` assertion, and the declaration-count coverage guard, together with removing `fetch-depth: 0`. After the third material draft correction exhausted the review budget, the maintainer directed a split and the predecessor was superseded. This slice removes exactly one behavior: the permanent historical mint regression that runs `git worktree add --detach … 6dd1d95` and the `BASE_COMMIT` constant in `src/grace-generate.test.ts`.
The retained current-code race test and its real-CLI, implicit-supersede, and exported-route variants drive the real CLI (or a Bun runner importing `mintResolvedBundle` / `mintBundle`) against a disposable project under an isolated-process preload that patches `node:fs.mkdirSync`, plants a competitor `spec.xml` and an unrelated file at the creation boundary **inside the spawned process**, and reports that it fired on stderr. The repaired engine acquires the candidate leaf with a non-recursive `mkdir` whose `EEXIST` refuses, so the competitor survives byte-for-byte.
The old-code checkout existed only to prove that refusal is not vacuous. The replacement is the same proof done once, on a disposable non-Git copy, and recorded here instead of shipped as a permanent suite member. Measured 2026-09-28 UTC on a copy of the repository at base `80cc36f789dc35ef789cfe6d753a39e7115dce76` with `node_modules` symlinked and no `.git`:
- baseline, restored file: `bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-generate.test.ts -t "AC-MINT-EXCLUSIVE: the repaired tree refuses"` exits 0, 1 pass. - mutation A (only the recursive `mkdir`: `mkdirSync(bundlePath, { recursive: true })`): the same command still exits 0, because the shipped `flag: "wx"` exclusive `spec.xml` write still refuses the existing competitor. Half the defect is masked; the red control must drive both halves. - mutation B (recursive `mkdir` together with the non-exclusive `writeFileSync(candidate.specPath, candidate.expectedSpecBytes)`, the pre-repair F314 pair): the same command exits 1 at `expect(result.exit, "the repaired leaf mkdir refuses").not.toBe(0)`, `Expected: not 0`. - restore: `cp` of the saved `src/grace-generate.ts` is byte-identical to the canonical file, and the same command exits 0 again.
The depth assertion stays because the declaration-count guard stays. `coverageRegressions` (`scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts:346`) reads `git show 2434fd467458e15c12414a74e37b09f9d71bdfd2:<path>` for every existing `*.test.ts`, so the `validate` job must keep `fetch-depth: 0` and `validateJobCheckoutDepth` must keep asserting it. Applied `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY` (`C-LINUX-VALIDATION-REPAIR-6-62765C22:712-729`) tied `fetch-depth: 0` to the `6dd1d95` control. This slice overturns that historical-control **purpose clause** — the control is gone — while **retaining** `fetch-depth: 0` and the guard for the count guard's base; the later sequential bundle retires the remaining full-depth mechanism. Only the assertion's test title was untrue after the `6dd1d95` control is gone — it named the pinned baseline control as the reason — so the title changes to `the validate job checks out full history for the declaration-count coverage guard's historical base`. Every other symbol in the file, including `COVERAGE_BASE`, `declaredTests`, `coverageRegressions`, `collectTestFiles`, the coverage test, and the `validate:ci` one-suite-run guard, is retained.
`test-metrics.json` is regenerated from an explicitly invalidated artifact with one measured `bun run test:metrics`, because `artifactIsStale` does not notice a deletion or a rename inside an existing test file. The retired mint test name and the old depth title disappear; the new title appears.
The mutation is not added to the suite and `src/grace-generate.test.ts` gains no planted-defect test. The permanent suite therefore carries the green direction and none of the mutation, which is the boundary the brief draws.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the predecessor's broad scope and also remove the depth assertion and the declaration-count guard. Rejected: it is not authorized by this slice, the count guard is still present and still reads a historical object, and the user wants those retirements in the next sequential bundle with `fetch-depth: 0`.

Keep the permanent `6dd1d95` checkout and its `BASE_COMMIT`. Rejected: the retained real-CLI race test plus the measured one-time two-part red control preserve discrimination without shipping an ancestor tree into every normal run.

Remove the coverage guard and the depth assertion now, in the same file already in scope. Rejected: it would leave `fetch-depth: 0` asserting a mechanism that no longer exists and would carry the next bundle's contract into this slice; the next bundle retires the three together.

Replace the historical checkout with a synthetic in-memory "old publisher" fixture that reproduces the pre-repair overwrite without Git. Rejected for this slice: it reimplements the defect as production-shaped test machinery and risks drifting from the real pre-repair code; the one-time mutation of the real file is the faithful control.

Leave `test-metrics.json` untouched because `artifactIsStale` will not red on a rename or a deletion inside a file. Rejected: the artifact would silently keep the retired mint test name and the false depth title. Regeneration is driven from a removed stale artifact, and the relation is pinned, not a duration.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The next sequential bundle after this close retires the declaration-count coverage guard, the retitled depth assertion, and `fetch-depth: 0` together, then regenerates metrics; its expected implementation paths are `scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts`, `.github/workflows/validate.yml`, and `test-metrics.json`. It answers applied `AC-COVERAGE-INTACT` and retires the remaining `AC-WORKFLOW-FULL-HISTORY` full-depth mechanism. This bundle neither mints nor authors it and does not claim those are retired.

Measured executed-code coverage is deferred to a later, separate small bundle, with its rationale recorded in project-specific memory outside this repository. This bundle keeps the weak declaration-count guard and adds no coverage tooling.

The concurrent-worker `ChangeDetector` design is not part of this artifact. Its future interface identifies changes between each dedicated worker workspace and its baseline, and Git is its first replaceable implementation. It belongs to its own concurrency artifact and does not affect this slice.

Scenarios.Scenario: A post-implementation checkout with the historical mint worktree operation gone: the normal mint regression suite runs the retained `spec new` race test, the implicit-supersede CLI test, and the two exported-route runner tests, refuses the interspersed competitor, preserves the competitor bytes, and spawns no `git worktree`. This says nothing about the declaration-count guard's history read: the guard still requires the full-history `validate` job with base `2434fd4…`, and if that base is absent it **fails open** — `git show` exits non-zero and `coverageRegressions` `continue`s — so an absent-base green is a fail-open result, never evidence that the guard checked declarations.

The metric refresh: the stale `test-metrics.json` is removed, one measured `bun run test:metrics` runs, and the result names the new depth title and neither the retired mint test name nor the old depth title, with the file list complete and the internal totals equal.

A post-close applied-archive tree: the historical mint test and `BASE_COMMIT` are gone, the depth assertion is retitled and passing, `.github/workflows/validate.yml` is byte-identical at the base, the declaration-count guard is intact and green under full history, lint is 0/0, and the narrow suites pass.
